text: Your phone says forty percent. You step outside... and it dies.

Winter in Germany. Minus five degrees.
You're checking when your train comes.
You go back inside, warm it up... and suddenly it says thirty percent again.

text: Wait. Did your battery just come back from the dead?

You see, a battery makes power with tiny chemical reactions.
In the cold, they slow down. Like you, trying to get out of bed on a January morning.
The energy is still there. The phone just can't get it out fast enough, so it shuts down to protect itself.
Apple says phones work best between zero and thirty-five degrees.
So keep it in your inside pocket.

text: Your phone hates winter as much as you do.
